introduction.description: Opens the email. Sets context, states what is being announced, and gives the reader a reason to keep reading.
rules: First sentence must state the course name or topic and its single most compelling benefit
Follow with 2–3 sentences that expand on why this matters to the reader right now
Close with a transition that leads naturally into the next component
Do not use a generic opener like 'We are excited to announce'
No bullet points — prose only
Write at least 60 words

hook.description: Grabs attention immediately. Used instead of introduction when urgency or a trend is the lead.
rules: Must create immediate relevance — reference a trend, a stat, a deadline, or a bold statement
Second sentence should deepen the hook — add context or a surprising detail
Third sentence (optional) bridges to the offer or course
No fluff — every word must earn its place
No bullet points — prose only
Write at least 40 words

story.description: Builds context or emotional connection. Bridges the hook to the offer.
rules: Open by establishing the real-world situation or trend
Build toward the reader's position — where are they now, what problem do they have?
Show how the course or offer is the natural next step
Close by transitioning to the offer, project list, or CTA
Write in second person — address the reader directly
No bullet points — prose only
Write at least 80 words

announcement.description: A direct, factual statement of what is new. Used for updates that need no sell.
rules: First sentence states what is new and when it is available
Follow with 1–2 sentences giving the key details — what it covers, what the student gets
Final sentence tells the reader where to find it or what to do next
No hype — factual and clear
Write at least 40 words

hero_image.description: The primary course banner image displayed at the top of the email.
rules: Use the course banner from assets/images/banners/
Preferred file: hero_banner.png
Always include alt text equal to the course name

course_image.description: A supporting course image — used in sale and update emails where a full hero is not needed.
rules: Use a pricing card or secondary banner from assets/images/
Smaller visual weight than hero_image — this is supporting, not primary

thumbnail_image.description: A video thumbnail shown in youtube_promotion emails. Renders with rounded corners. Do not include any play button overlays.
rules: Always wrap the image in a div with position:relative, border-radius:12px, overflow:hidden, and line-height:0
Always apply 24px left and right padding on the outer cell so the rounded corners are visible against the email background
Always link the entire block to the YouTube video URL
Never overlay a play button.
Always include a one-line caption below the image in font-size:12px; color:#AAAAAA; text-align:center

gif_demo.description: An animated GIF showing a project from the course in action.
rules: Always use files from assets/gifs/ — never from assets/videos/
Pick the most visually impressive demo available in that folder
Prefer a demo that shows the end result, not the process
Include a one-line caption describing what is being shown
Use a standard img tag — never a video tag

code_screenshot.description: A screenshot showing a key or interesting piece of code from the lesson.
rules: Only use if the code snippet is visually clean and short enough to be readable in an email
Include a one-line caption explaining what the code does

output_fields.caption: one sentence describing what the code does

meme.description: A relevant GIF or meme fetched from KLIPY based on the campaign mood. Used to add personality, humor, and emotional tone to an email.

api.auth: API key embedded in the URL path — no header needed

rules: Determine the campaign mood from the campaign type and email role
Use the mood_to_query_map to pick a search query — pick the most fitting one
Prefer the Meme API for humorous/relatable content — use GIF API for more animated/expressive content
Call the API, get the results, and pick the first result with a usable direct image URL
Use the medium or downsized format for email — never the original full size
Never use memes or GIFs that contain real named people or celebrities
Must be appropriate for a professional-but-casual audience — no crude or offensive content
Include a short caption below the image that ties it back to the email message
Save the selected item ID and URL in the campaign brief under the relevant email entry

output_fields.asset_url: direct image URL from KLIPY response
output_fields.caption: one short sentence connecting the meme to the email message
output_fields.klipy_id: item id from response — save for reference

meme.html_output: See html_output pattern in AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md — centered img at 400px with caption below in #AAAAAA Arial 13px

what_you_will_learn.description: A bullet list of specific skills the student will gain.
rules: Always open with one intro sentence before the list — e.g. 'Here is what you will be able to do by the end of this course:'
Each item must be a specific, concrete skill — not a vague outcome
Each item should be a full sentence, not a fragment — aim for 10–15 words per item
Start each item with a verb: 'Build', 'Deploy', 'Train', 'Connect', 'Create'
No item should repeat or overlap with another

what_you_will_build.description: A numbered list of real projects the student will build, displayed as blue numbered badge + bold project name + short gray description. Section label is 'What You Will Build' in blue uppercase.
rules: Always render as a vertically stacked numbered list with blue badge icons — never as a prose list or plain bullets
Section label must be 'What You Will Build' in blue (#1A6DAF) uppercase letter-spacing
Follow the label with one bold intro sentence summarising the total count and scope of projects
Use the actual project names from the course_file.md — do not invent names
Each item has: a 22×22px blue (#1A6DAF) rounded (6px) number badge, a bold dark project name, and a 1-sentence gray description
Description is 10–15 words, color #777777, explaining what the project does and why it is impressive
Last item has padding-bottom:0 — all others have padding-bottom:14px

html_format.section_label: What You Will Build
html_format.intro_sentence: {intro}
html_format.number_badge: {n}

output_fields.intro: one bold sentence with total project count and scope

features.description: A bullet list of key selling points or course features.
rules: Focus on what makes this course different — not generic benefits
Pull from the Key Benefits section of the course_file.md
Each item should be one line — no sub-bullets

facts_numbers.description: Social proof stats displayed as a 2-column icon grid. Section label is 'Why CVZone' in blue uppercase. Each stat has a blue rounded emoji icon, a bold title, and a short gray description.
rules: Always render as a 2×2 grid of icon+title+description items — never as a prose list
Section label must always be 'Why CVZone' in blue (#1A6DAF) uppercase letter-spacing
Each item has: a 36×36px blue (#1A6DAF) rounded (8px) emoji icon box, a bold dark title, and a short gray description
Use real numbers only — from the course_file.md or brand_document.md social proof section
Each item title must be short and punchy — e.g. '80+ Countries', '#1 on Google', '1M+ Students', '100% Positive'
Description is 1 sentence max, color #777777

html_format.section_label: Why CVZone
html_format.grid: 2-column table, each cell width:50%. Left column padding-right:12px, right column padding-left:12px. Each row padding-bottom:18px.
html_format.icon_box: {emoji}
html_format.title: {title}

output_fields.items: array of 4 objects: { emoji, title, description }

pricing.description: Displays course pricing as a row of individual cards — one card per tier. Section label is 'Sale Pricing' in blue uppercase. Each card shows plan name, strike-through original price, sale price, 'Save $X' in blue, a divider, and 2–3 feature lines with ✓ checkmarks. The most popular tier gets a blue border and a blue 'Most Popular' header band.
rules: Appears ONCE per email as its own standalone section — NEVER embed pricing cards inside a cta block
Always render as individual side-by-side cards — never as a single bordered table
Section label must be 'Sale Pricing' in blue (#1A6DAF) uppercase letter-spacing
Follow with a subtitle: 'Choose your tier — all plans include lifetime access'
Each card: light gray background (#F8F8F8), border 1px solid #EEEEEE, border-radius 12px
Most popular card: border 2px solid #1A6DAF, blue (#1A6DAF) header band with '★ Most Popular' in white, plan name in blue instead of gray
Strike-through original price in #AAAAAA, sale price in #111111 at 28px bold, 'Save $X' in #1A6DAF bold
Feature divider: border-top 1px solid #EEEEEE, features in #777777 with ✓ prefix
Always show the coupon code if provided — display below the cards as: 'Use code {CODE} at checkout'
Always include: 'Lifetime access on all plans · 3-day money-back guarantee' below the cards
Always show original price alongside sale price

html_format.section_label: Sale Pricing
html_format.subtitle: Choose your tier — all plans include lifetime access
html_format.card_standard: background-color:#F8F8F8; border:1px solid #EEEEEE; border-radius:12px; overflow:hidden — inner padding:20px 18px 18px
html_format.card_popular: background-color:#F8F8F8; border:2px solid #1A6DAF; border-radius:12px; overflow:hidden — blue header band + inner padding:16px 18px 18px
html_format.popular_band: ★ Most Popular
html_format.plan_name_standard: {name}
html_format.plan_name_popular: {name}
html_format.features:
✓ {feature1}
✓ {feature2}
✓ {feature3}
html_format.coupon_line: Use code {CODE} at checkout  ·  Lifetime access on all plans  ·  3-day money-back guarantee

cta.description: A call to action button. May appear multiple times in one email — the same button text and URL is used each time, placed at different points to catch readers at different stages of engagement.
rules: Text must be action-oriented — start with a verb
Link must go to the specific course page, not the homepage
Never use vague text like 'Click Here' or 'Submit'
Match the CTA text to the campaign type as defined in campaign_types.md
When the sequence includes two CTAs, both must use identical text and URL — do not vary the message
The final CTA in the email is always a standalone full-width button
For youtube_promotion campaigns, always use a red background (#CC4444) for the CTA button

limited_time_offer.description: An urgency block explaining the deadline and reinforcing the value of acting now.
rules: Only generate this component if a real deadline or limit exists
First sentence states the exact end date or time of the offer
Follow with a sentence reinforcing what the reader gets if they act now
Optional: add a sentence about what happens after the deadline (price goes back up)
Do not manufacture urgency — if no deadline is provided, do not invent one
Write at least 35 words

countdown.description: A live animated GIF countdown timer generated via the CountdownMail API. Updates on every email open.
rules: Only include if the user provides a real end date — never invent a deadline
Always call the CountdownMail API to create the timer before writing the email HTML
Use the end_date from campaign_brief.md as the time_end value
Always use the exact color values defined in api_request_body — never change them
Always set expired_mes_on to 1 and expired_mes to 'This offer has expired'
Place immediately before the CTA component
Save the returned timer code in campaign_brief.md under Generation Log
Always wrap the img in the overflow:hidden div defined in html_output — this hides the CountdownMail attribution text

api_request_body.name: campaign name from campaign_brief.md
api_request_body.time_end: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS from campaign end date
api_request_body.time_zone: use timezone provided by user, default UTC

api_response.src: GIF URL — use as img src in email HTML

countdown.html_output: Sale Ends In

bonus.description: Extra items included with a purchase or bootcamp enrollment.
rules: Only include if bonus items are explicitly provided by the user
Each item should name the bonus and its value in one line
Do not invent bonuses
